correctness.rationale: For each binary target the objective is a piecewise-linear circle-distance function. The explicit piecewise formulas for targets \(010\) and \(111\) show that, beyond the bounded small range, a minimizer is one of the two grid points adjacent to \(1/4\); direct substitution gives their four residue classes. The other six targets have explicit continuous witnesses of error at most \(1/5\), and the objective is \(3\)-Lipschitz, so for \(N\ge30\) their nearest grid points have error at most \(1/4\). Exact finite enumeration closes \(5\le N\le29\). The bundled verifier uses exact integer arithmetic and checks all eight targets through \(N=200\); an independent reconstruction of the same minimization through \(N=80\) reproduced every stated value.

originality.rationale: Hare and Ramsey determine continuous-circle Kronecker constants for three-element integer sets and, in particular, the continuous binary angular value \(1/4\) for the three-term arithmetic progression. Their approximation parameter ranges over the full circle. The audited theorem instead restricts that parameter to the finite subgroup \(N^{-1}\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z\) and derives an exact mod-four discretization penalty for every grid size. Neither the continuous value nor the general three-element classification implies those finite-grid residue classes.
residual_risks: An equivalent finite-cyclic formula could exist under harmonic-analysis or coding terminology not captured by the bounded searches.

value.rationale: Restricting a continuous Kronecker approximation problem to finite cyclic characters is a natural discretization, and the theorem quantifies the exact sampling loss for every grid size rather than computing a single small case. The residue-class law explains precisely when the finite problem reaches the continuous optimum and how fast it approaches it otherwise.
residual_risks: The result is confined to one three-term arithmetic progression.

final_claim: For every \(N\ge5\), the binary angular Kronecker radius of \(\{1,2,3\}\) when the approximating phase is restricted to the cyclic grid \(N^{-1}\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z\) is \(1/4\) for \(N\equiv0\pmod4\), \((N+2)/(4N)\) for \(N\equiv2\pmod4\), and \((N+3)/(4N)\) for odd \(N\); the two target patterns \(010\) and \(111\) determine the maximum with the stated residue-class formulas.
limitations: Only the spectrum \(\{1,2,3\}\), binary target phases, and angular distance are covered.
The theorem is not a classification of arbitrary three-character subsets or chordal Kronecker constants.
